h1:
Rayong Fruit-Season Plan
Durian, Rambutan & Mangosteen Orchards
intro: Rayong is one of the most fun provinces in eastern Thailand when fruit season hits. As the early rains arrive, Monthong durian, rambutan and mangosteen all come in together, and many orchards let you walk through, pick fresh, and sit down to an all-you-can-eat buffet under the trees. We've laid this out as a 2-day, 1-night plan, working from the Taphong–Khao Yai Da area near the city out to the bigger orchards around Wang Chan and Ban Khai. If you only have one day, just take Day 1.

blocks.html: Before you plan, get a feel for the fruit timing. Rayong's Monthong durian is well known (it even holds GI status), and the stretch when fruit comes in thick and orchards run lively buffets is roughly mid-April through about July. Rambutan and mangosteen usually follow in May–June. Some orchards open only during fruit season; others stay open year-round but only have the full spread during these months. So if you want a buffet of fresh fruit, aim for this window and always call the orchard ahead, since yields and prices shift with the season.

blocks.title: Check before you set off
blocks.html: Most orchards ask you to call to book or confirm a slot ahead of time, especially on long weekends, because buffet sittings fill up fast and certain fruits can sell out for the day. The prices we list are rough figures from past seasons — use them only for a ballpark comparison.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Taphong & Khao Yai Da, the orchards near town

blocks.html: Day one covers the area closest to downtown Rayong: Taphong sub-district and Khao Yai Da. This zone is only about 15–20 minutes from the city, with several fruit orchards lined up one after another — an easy way to open the trip without a long drive.

items.activity: Leave downtown Rayong and head for Taphong sub-district
items.note: Fill up on fuel and coffee first — signal can be patchy in spots inside the orchards

items.activity: Visit Suan Yai Da–Je Boonchuen (Taphong) for a morning walk-and-taste fruit buffet
items.note: A long-running buffet orchard that plenty of people know, with durian, rambutan, mangosteen and salak. Buffet roughly 350–450 THB/adult · open around 09:00–17:00 · call ahead to book a slot

items.activity: Take a break and find lunch around Taphong
items.note: Don't fill up entirely on fruit in the morning — save room for a real meal and for the next orchard

items.activity: Stop by Taphong Fruit Market to grab some durian and mangosteen to take home
items.note: Taphong Fruit Market is the area's hub for fresh fruit, and retail prices are usually cheaper than buying in town. You can have the vendor cut one open to check before you buy

items.activity: Drive up Khao Yai Da for orchard viewpoints and a cafe with garden views
items.note: Khao Yai Da has spots that overlook the wide fruit-orchard fields, and in the late afternoon the light softens for nice photos

items.activity: Head back to check in at a hotel in Rayong town or at Mae Ramphueng Beach
items.note: Staying in town makes it easy to find dinner, while Mae Ramphueng Beach is the call if you'd rather sleep near the sea tonight

blocks.title: How to eat fruit without overdoing it
blocks.html: Durian is rich and 'heaty' — eat it alternating with cooler mangosteen, sip water steadily, and don't dig in on a totally empty stomach. That way you can keep going all day without feeling stuffed.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Wang Chan & Ban Khai, the bigger orchards out of town

blocks.html: Day two heads out to the larger orchards a bit further from the city, over toward Wang Chan and Ban Khai districts. The orchards here are spacious, and some run full-on buffet festivals with garden activities to wander and take photos. Figure on about 40–60 minutes' drive from town depending on the spot.

items.activity: Check out, then head for Wang Chan district
items.note: The main route uses Highway 344 (Ban Bueng–Klaeng), an easy drive

items.activity: Enter Suan Lamai (Wang Chan) for a durian and mixed-fruit buffet sitting
items.note: Suan Lamai runs a buffet festival during durian season (around Apr–Jun) with Monthong durian, rambutan, mangosteen, longkong, salak, and processed treats like fried durian · adults roughly 800 THB, kids discounted · you can book a slot online ahead of time

items.activity: Leave Wang Chan and head over to Ban Khai district
items.note: Grab a light lunch on the way to give your stomach a break from all the fruit

items.activity: Visit Supattra Land (Ban Khai) and take the tram tour past more than 20 kinds of fruit
items.note: An agritourism orchard that's open most of the year, with an entry/tram fee, and a separate buffet during fruit season · good for families, with pretty gardens to stroll and photograph

items.activity: Buy boxed fruit and souvenirs before heading home
items.note: Many orchards have a counter selling graded fruit and processed goods like durian paste and fried durian to bring back for people at home
Coming from Bangkok, the motorway–Highway 36 route is easy. Allow extra time for heavy traffic on weekend evenings

items: Monthong durian — Rayong's star, coming in thick from around mid-April to June. Thick, dry flesh that's sweet and creamy, and a registered GI product of the province
Mangosteen — follows in May–June, with deep-purple skin and white flesh that's sweet-tart. Pair it with durian to cut the richness
Rambutan — shows up in May–July, with the Rongrien variety having flesh that peels clean off the seed, sweet and crisp. A favorite with kids
Longkong, salak & langsat — supporting fruits many orchards add to the buffet, around the same window as rambutan and mangosteen

blocks.html: If the rains come early or late in a given year, the fruit window can shift by a week or two. If you want early-season durian while prices are still high, go in early April. If you want easier-on-the-wallet prices and the full range of fruit, May–June is the sweet spot.

blocks.text: What to prep before an orchard visit

items.name: Bring cash
items.blurb: Many orchards take cash more readily than transfers, especially the fruit market and roadside stalls — keep some on hand

items.name: Wear orchard-friendly shoes
items.blurb: Orchard ground can get muddy in the rainy season, so shoes that can get wet and won't slip will be more comfortable

items.name: Go in the morning
items.blurb: The fruit is fresh, the crowds are thin and the sun isn't harsh — a morning slot around 9–10am is the best time

faq.q: When is fruit season for orchard visits in Rayong?
faq.a: The stretch when fruit comes in thick and orchards run buffets is roughly mid-April through about July. Monthong durian arrives first, followed by mangosteen and rambutan in May–June. The timing can shift year to year with the rains, so it's best to call the orchard before you go.

faq.q: How much does a Rayong fruit buffet cost?
faq.a: It depends on the orchard and the time of season. Several orchards in the Taphong area start around 350–450 THB per adult, while a full-scale durian buffet festival like Suan Lamai runs higher, around 800 THB per adult, with kids usually discounted. These are ballpark figures — check with the orchard again.

faq.q: Is one day enough to visit Rayong's fruit orchards?
faq.a: Yes, if you stick to the Taphong–Khao Yai Da area near town, which is only 15–20 minutes' drive. You can hit 1–2 orchards plus the fruit market in a single day. But if you also want the bigger orchards around Wang Chan–Ban Khai, staying one night makes it more relaxed.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead to visit Rayong's fruit orchards?
faq.a: Orchards that run buffet sittings generally recommend booking or confirming a slot ahead, especially on long weekends, since sittings fill up fast and some fruits sell out for the day. Walking around to buy fruit at the market doesn't need a booking.

faq.q: Can I visit Rayong's orchards without my own car?
faq.a: Most fruit orchards sit off the public transport routes, so having your own car or hiring one with a driver is the most convenient option, since you'll be moving between Taphong, Wang Chan and Ban Khai, which lie in different directions.
